newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish quiet day mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish quiet day mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a quiet session mixed, with the Swiss franc dominating action.
March Swiss francs set a fresh contract low midday at $0.7555, below the old low at $0.7568, as traders eyed strength in sterling versus Swiss.

Traders also looked to a report that commercial bankruptcies in Switzerland rose 9.6 percent in the 11 months to November 30 compared with the same period last year. Traders said such news did not bode well for the Swiss unit.
Traders said bullish dollar sentiment reverberated through currency markets, also keeping Swiss and marks under pressure.

March Swiss rebounded from its lows late in the day, along with March marks, as light buying entered the thin pre-holiday trading pits. Traders said a few buy orders helped trigger a swift move back to the middle of the range.

"It was relatively uneventful trade," one IMM trader said. "We ran through some stops on the downside early in Swiss and marks and I thought we'd get to $0.6460 in marks, but we never got there," he said.
He said the market could face choppy action and thin pits as the Christmans and New Year holidays approached.
March sterling rose to the highest price since December 3 after bullish news overnight, but closed off its session high.
UK November unemployment fell a robust 95,800 to below the psychologically key two-million level. Stronger-than-expected UK retail sales further stoked hopes for a hike in interest rates.
Traders said sterling continued to garner support from the notion that it was the safe-haven currency for EMU concerns, which also hindered Swiss.
Analysts said a firm U.S. stock market on Wednesday also helped the dollar.

At settlement, March yen was up $0.000014 to $0.008908, marks fell $0.0010 to $0.6479, Swiss francs lost $0.0031 to $0.7579, Sterling jumped $0.0032 to $1.6704, Canadian dollar fell $0.0016 to $0.7356, Australian dollar lost $0.0039 to $0.7909, and Mexican peso lost $0.000200 to $0.120900.
